article.headline: CPSC Warns Parents to Stop Using WPX-4 Slide Playsets — 17-Month-Old Died in Entrapment Incident

research.facts:
WPX-4 Slide Playset CPSC Warning
**Sources:** CPSC.gov official warning, Click2Houston, The Hill
**Key facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Product: Model WPX-4 Slide Playsets — indoor/outdoor plastic playsets with tunnel, slide, and basketball hoop
- Manufacturer: Wenzhou Yidian Amusement Equipment Co., Ltd. (China)
- Hazard: Multiple openings where a child's torso can pass through but the head cannot — head and neck entrapment risk
- Incident: 1 confirmed death — a 17-month-old child died in an entrapment incident
- CPSC action: This is a WARNING issued August 13, 2026 — CPSC urges consumers to stop use immediately and DISPOSE of the product
- Critical: Do NOT sell or give away — the product should be destroyed/disposed
- No refund mechanism announced yet (this is a warning, not a formal recall with remedy)
- URL: CPSC.gov warning page issued August 13, 2026

article.headline: Goody King Magnetic Building Cubes Recalled — 213,500 Units Sold on Amazon, 2 Children Required Surgery

research.facts:
Goody King Magnetic Building Cubes Recall
**Sources:** CPSC.gov official recall, ABC News, Fox Business
**Key facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Product: Goody King-branded Magnetic Building Cubes and Blocks
- Importer: Yi Suen Commerce, Hong Kong
- Units: approximately 213,500
- Sets: 45, 56, 100, 120, 150, and 300 cubes; themed (forests, dinosaurs, unicorns)
- Sold: exclusively on Amazon.com between January 2024 and July 2026
- Hazard: Cubes can break or open, exposing high-powered magnets; if 2+ magnets swallowed, they attract through intestinal walls causing perforations, twisting, or blockage — can cause blood poisoning and death
- Incidents: At least 27 reports of cubes breaking; 2 children required surgery to remove swallowed magnets
- Action: Stop use immediately; contact Yi Suen Commerce for full refund; company sends prepaid shipping label after consumer registers for recall; refund issued after company receives returned product
- Recall date: August 13, 2026

article.headline: Jenkins Middle School Reopens After 18 Months — D11 Students Return to New 20-Classroom Wing

research.facts:
Jenkins Middle School Reopening
**Sources:** FOX21, KRDO, KKTV
**Key facts (HIGH confidence):**
- School: Jenkins Middle School, D11
- Ribbon cutting: August 12, 2026, at 8:15 AM (same day as D11 first day of school)
- Grades: 6th, 7th, and 8th graders returned to the Jenkins campus
- Closure reason: Cracking and separating floors and walls; original building never properly anchored to foundation
- During 2025-26 school year: 6th and 7th graders in portable classrooms in Jenkins parking lot; 8th graders attended Doherty High School
- New construction: Demolished 7th and 8th grade wing; built new wing on stable ground; 20,000 square feet; 20 new classrooms (10 per floor); building newly anchored to foundation
- Groundbreaking: October 2025

article.headline: Palmer High School's $100M Renovation Is Underway — What COS Families Need to Know

research.facts:
Palmer High $100M Renovation
**Sources:** KRDO, KOAA, Colorado Springs Gazette
**Key facts (HIGH confidence):**
- School: Palmer High School, D11 — Colorado Springs' oldest high school, founded 1874
- Project: $100 million renovation of campus; Phase 1 completion early spring 2028
- Funding: Certificate of participation funds
- Phase 1 scope: Demolish current tech building and cafeteria; construct new academic wing
- Boulder Street: Permanently closed after City Council reversed initial vote in May 2026; allows D11 to unite both halves of campus
- Campus status: Fully open and operational during construction; modular classrooms moved to campus
- Traffic: Families driving near downtown COS should expect construction zone congestion
- Additional: 12 new school zones being established at middle and high schools across Colorado Springs (HIGH confidence — KRDO Aug 11)
